q: Were the school council to approve the treehouse plan, building ___ next term.
explain: 'Were + subject + to + verb' is a formal unreal 'if', so the result uses would + verb. Example: Were it to snow, school would close.

notes.will begin: Will begin is a real future; this is a hypothetical.
notes.began: Began is past and doesn't fit 'next term'.
notes.had begun: Had begun is past perfect, not a result form.

q: Little ___ that the castle had been watching them.
explain: After negative words like Little at the start, invert: did + subject + verb. Example: Little did I expect a surprise party.

notes.they knew: Normal order isn't allowed after a fronted 'Little'.
notes.they did know: 'They did know' still has subject first.
notes.knew they: 'Knew they' needs did: did they know.

q: Only after the gates had closed ___ their mistake.
explain: 'Only after...' at the start triggers inversion in the main clause. Example: Only after dinner did we open the presents.

notes.they realised: Normal order isn't allowed after 'Only after...'.
notes.realised they: 'Realised they' isn't inversion; we need did.

q: It's essential that every team member ___ at practice on Saturday.
explain: After essential/vital/important that, formal English uses the plain verb (subjunctive) for everyone. Example: It's vital that he be on time.

notes.is being: Is being is continuous and not the subjunctive.
notes.will be: Will be isn't used after 'essential that' in formal style.

q: ___ the heavy rain, the sports day went ahead.
explain: Despite + noun (no 'of'). Example: Despite the noise, I slept.

notes.Although: Although needs a clause: Although it rained heavily.
notes.However: However joins two sentences: It rained. However, ...
notes.In spite: In spite needs 'of': in spite of the rain.

q: The robot design, ___ merits are obvious, was rejected by the judges.
explain: Whose shows possession for things too. Example: a book whose cover is torn.

notes.of which: Of which would need 'the merits of which'.

q: She'd sooner quit the team than ___ the truth.
explain: Would sooner X than Y: both verbs are plain forms. Example: I'd sooner walk than wait.

q: Not only ___ the class promise, but he also broke it.
explain: Not only at the start → inversion: did he sign. Example: Not only did she win, she also broke the record.

notes.he signed: Normal order isn't allowed after 'Not only'.
notes.signed he: 'Signed he' is old-fashioned and wrong here.

q: Hardly had the school play started ___ the lights went out.
explain: Hardly had... when (no sooner had... than). Example: Hardly had I sat down when the phone rang.

notes.then: Then isn't used in this pattern.
notes.that: That isn't used in this pattern.

q: Should you need assistance, ___ hesitate to ask.
explain: 'Should you...' = if you...; the instruction is an imperative: don't + verb. Example: Should you get lost, don't panic.

notes.not: Not alone can't make an imperative.
notes.no: No isn't used before a verb like this.

q: The inventor is said ___ the discovery years before anyone else.
explain: Is said to have + past participle reports something earlier. Example: She's said to have learned five languages.

notes.to make: To make is about now or the future.
notes.that made: That made needs 'It is said that...'.

q: What I find most frustrating ___ the lack of save points in this game.
explain: A What-clause subject is singular: What I need is... Example: What I love is the music.

notes.are: Are is plural; the What-clause is singular.
notes.to be: To be isn't a finite verb.

q: Rarely ___ such eloquence at a school assembly.
explain: Fronted Rarely → inversion with an auxiliary. Example: Rarely have I seen such snow.

q: It was the knight's courage, rather than his skill, ___ won the day.
explain: A cleft sentence: It was X that... Example: It was the dog that ate it.

notes.who: Who would need a person; courage is a thing.

q: Had it not been for her quick thinking, the sandcastle ___.
explain: Had it not been for... = without (past); result: would have + past participle. Example: Had it not been for you, I'd have failed.

notes.had collapsed: Had failed isn't a result form.

q: So convincing ___ that the teacher changed her mind.
explain: So + adjective at the start → inversion: was her argument. Example: So loud was the music that we left.

notes.her argument was: Normal order isn't allowed after a fronted 'So convincing'.
notes.did her argument: Did doesn't go with an adjective here.

q: Not until much later ___ how big the comet really was.
explain: Not until... at the start → did + subject + verb. Example: Not until I got home did I notice.

q: ___ as it may seem, the plan actually worked.
explain: Adjective + as + it may seem = although it seems... Example: Odd as it sounds, it's true.

notes.Strangely: An adverb can't start this pattern.

q: The vet recommended that the injured owl ___ kept indoors for a week.
explain: Recommend that + plain verb (subjunctive). Example: I suggest that he rest.

notes.will be: Will be isn't used after 'recommend that'.

q: What our team needs ___ fewer excuses and more practice.
explain: What-clauses take a singular verb. Example: What I want is a dog.

q: ___ the clues, the young detectives had no choice but to free the parrot.
explain: Given = considering. Example: Given the weather, we stayed in.

notes.Giving: Giving would mean they gave something.
notes.To give: To give doesn't start this clause.
notes.Having given: Having given means they gave it.

q: On no account ___ the gates be left open after dark.
explain: On no account → inversion with a modal: should the gates be. Example: On no account should you feed the dragon.

notes.must not: Must not adds a double negative.

q: She is thought ___ with the dragons in secret for years before peace was agreed.
explain: Is thought to have been + -ing = a long action earlier. Example: He's thought to have been living abroad.

notes.to negotiate: To build is present or future.
notes.negotiating: Negotiating doesn't follow 'is thought'; it needs 'to'.
notes.to be negotiated: To be negotiated is passive: she isn't the thing being negotiated.

q: ___ the project been better presented, it might have won.
explain: Had + subject + past participle = if... had (third conditional). Example: Had I known, I'd have come.

notes.If: If needs 'had': If the project had been.

q: Much as I respect my coach's experience, I ___ with his plan.
explain: Much as = although. The second clause contrasts. Example: Much as I like it, I can't afford it.

q: The more clues emerged, ___ the villain's story became.
explain: The more..., the + comparative. Example: The more you read, the better you write.

notes.more weak: More weak is wrong for a short adjective.

q: It's high time the class ___ responsibility for the messy garden.
explain: It's high time + past simple. Example: It's high time we left.

notes.take: Present take isn't used after 'high time'.

q: Only when the dragons and knights made peace ___ relax.
explain: Only when... at the start → inversion: could the engineers. Example: Only when it stopped could we go out.

notes.the envoys did: Did doesn't fit with relax here.

q: Were the new motorway plan ___, the forest animals would lose their homes.
explain: Were + subject + to + verb = a formal unreal 'if'. Example: Were the match to go ahead, we'd play.

q: Not a word of complaint ___ from her during the whole hike.
explain: Negative object at the start → inversion: did we hear. Example: Not a sound did we make.

q: Seldom ___ a comet so bright from our school observatory.
explain: Negative/limiting adverb first (seldom, rarely, never) → auxiliary + subject. Example: Seldom have I laughed so much.

notes.we have seen: After seldom at the start we invert: have we.
notes.we saw: Past simple needs did: did we see.
notes.did we saw: Did is followed by the base form: see.

q: Under no circumstances ___ the dragon eggs be touched.
explain: Under no circumstances + auxiliary + subject. Example: Under no circumstances should you leave.

notes.you should: The auxiliary must come before the subject after this phrase.
notes.must not: The phrase is already negative, so no not.
notes.don't: Don't can't go before 'the dragon eggs be'.

q: At no point ___ that the robot would actually work.
explain: At no point + inversion with do/does/did. Example: At no point did she complain.

notes.anyone imagined: After at no point we invert.
notes.anyone did imagine: The auxiliary must come first: did anyone.
notes.imagined anyone: We need an auxiliary, not the main verb, before the subject.

q: Only later ___ that the map had been drawn upside down.
explain: Only + time expression first → inversion. Example: Only then did I understand.

notes.noticed the explorers: The main verb can't go before the subject here.
notes.had noticed the explorers: Had noticed the explorers puts the subject after the participle.

q: Scarcely had the bell rung ___ the students raced outside.
explain: Scarcely/hardly/barely had … when. Example: Barely had we sat down when the phone rang.

notes.then: Then isn't used in this pattern.

q: No sooner ___ the castle gates than it began to snow.
explain: No sooner + had + subject + p.p. + than. Example: No sooner had I sat down than the bell rang.

notes.we had reached: After no sooner we invert: had we.
notes.did we reach: The pattern uses the past perfect.
notes.we reached: No inversion: past simple doesn't fit here.

q: So loud ___ that the bats flew out of the cave.
explain: So + adjective first → be + subject. Example: So bright was the moon that we could read.

notes.the explosion was: After so + adjective at the start we invert.
notes.had the explosion: Had the explosion would need a past participle.

q: Such ___ her enthusiasm that the whole class joined the chess club.
explain: Such + be + noun + that = it was so great that. Example: Such was the noise that we left.

notes.is being: Is being doesn't fit a past story.

q: Not once ___ the captain lose her temper during the storm.
explain: Not once + did + subject + base verb. Example: Not once did he thank me.

notes.was: Was would need losing, which changes the meaning.

q: Little ___ that the quiet new girl was a chess champion.
explain: Little + did + subject + verb = we had no idea. Example: Little did he realise the danger.

notes.we suspected: After little at the start we invert.
notes.suspected we: The main verb can't come first.

q: Were the comet ___ closer, we would see it without a telescope.
explain: Were + subject + to-infinitive = If + past (formal). Example: Were it to rain, we'd stay inside.

notes.passing: Passing doesn't follow were here in a conditional.

q: ___ we not found the shortcut, we'd still be in the maze.
explain: Had + subject + not + p.p. = If … hadn't (third conditional). Example: Had I not stopped, I'd have fallen.

notes.If: If would need had: If we had not found.
notes.Were: Were is for present imaginary situations.
notes.Should: Should is for possible future events.

q: Should anyone ___ the secret password, the vault will lock.
explain: Should + subject + base verb = if (formal). Example: Should you need help, call me.

notes.guesses: After should we use the base form, no -es.

q: On no account ___ to feed the gremlins after midnight.
explain: On no account + inversion. Example: On no account must you open it.

notes.you are: After on no account we invert.
notes.do you: Do you to feed isn't English.

q: ___ I love most about astronomy is the feeling of wonder.
explain: Wh-cleft: What + clause + is … Example: What I need is a nap.

notes.That: That can't start a cleft clause like this.
notes.Which: Which needs a noun before it.
notes.It: It-clefts take the form 'It is … that'.

q: It was my grandma ___ taught me to play chess.
explain: It-cleft: It is/was + person + who/that. Example: It was Tom who broke it.

notes.whom she: Whom she adds an extra subject.
notes.what: What can't follow a noun in a cleft.

q: It wasn't until the lights went out ___ we saw the glowing fungi.
explain: It wasn't until … that = only at that moment. Example: It wasn't until I got home that I noticed.

notes.when: The cleft pattern uses that, not when.
notes.then: Then isn't used in this pattern.

q: All ___ want for my birthday is a telescope.
explain: All (that) I want is… = the only thing. Example: All we need is time.

notes.what I: All what I is not standard English.

q: The reason ___ the bridge collapsed was a tiny crack.
explain: The reason why/that + clause + was … Example: The reason why I'm late is the bus.

notes.because: The reason … was because repeats the idea.
notes.that's: That's would add a second verb.

q: ___ happened next astonished the whole class.
explain: What + clause as a subject. Example: What she said made me laugh.

notes.That: That happened next isn't a complete subject here.
notes.It: It would need a different structure: It astonished…
notes.Which: Which needs a noun before it.

q: The coach insisted that every player ___ a helmet.
explain: Subjunctive after insist/demand/recommend that: base verb for all persons. Example: I suggest that he leave.

notes.wore: Wore is past; the subjunctive uses the base form.

q: It's vital that the hamster ___ fresh water every day.
explain: It's vital/essential that + base verb (subjunctive). Example: It's essential that she be on time.

q: The head teacher proposed that the trip ___ until spring.
explain: Passive subjunctive: that + be + p.p. Example: They demanded that he be removed.

notes.be postpone: We need the past participle: postponed.
notes.postponed: Postponed alone suggests it already happened.

q: If the wizard ___ here, he would know the spell.
explain: If + were for imaginary present (all persons, formal). Example: If I were you, I'd rest.

notes.is: Is would be a real possibility.
notes.would be: Would doesn't go in the if-clause.
notes.be: Be is the subjunctive for 'that' clauses, not if.

q: She acts as if she ___ the queen of the playground.
explain: As if + past (were) for something untrue. Example: He talks as if he knew everything.

notes.is being: Is being suggests a temporary behaviour, not an unreal comparison.
notes.would be: Would be doesn't follow as if here.
notes.has been: Has been means it was true.

q: Suppose the robot ___ to malfunction during the show. What then?
explain: Suppose/Supposing + were to = an imaginary future. Example: Suppose you were to win.

notes.is going: Is going would need to: is going to.

q: If it ___ for the sheepdog, the lambs would have wandered off.
explain: If it hadn't been for = without (past). Example: If it hadn't been for you, I'd have failed.

notes.wasn't: Wasn't is for the present: If it wasn't for…
notes.isn't: Isn't is a real present situation.

q: I'd sooner you ___ the class pet over the holidays.
explain: I'd sooner/rather + person + past simple = preference about now. Example: I'd sooner you didn't go.

notes.look after: The base form doesn't follow I'd sooner + person.

q: You ___ have warned me the soup was so spicy!
explain: Might/could have + p.p. = mild criticism (you should have). Example: You might have told me!

notes.must: Must have is a deduction, not criticism.
notes.would rather: Would rather have isn't used for criticism.

q: We ___ have taken the shortcut. The path was flooded.
explain: Couldn't have + p.p. = it wasn't possible. Example: We couldn't have known.

notes.needn't: Needn't have = it wasn't necessary, but we did it.

q: The fossil ___ have belonged to a baby dinosaur, judging by its size.
explain: May well have + p.p. = it's quite likely. Example: She may well have left already.

notes.must not: Must not isn't used for past deduction.
notes.ought: Ought needs to: ought to have.

q: I ___ go to the party, but I'd rather finish my model.
explain: Might as well = there's no strong reason not to. Example: We might as well start now.

notes.had better: Had better is a warning; it doesn't fit 'but I'd rather'.
notes.would sooner: Would sooner means prefer, which contradicts 'but I'd rather'.
notes.may well not: May well not means it's likely I won't.

q: You ___ better hand in your project today, or you'll lose marks.
explain: Had better + base verb = strong advice with a warning. Example: You'd better hurry.

q: He ___ to have finished the puzzle by now, but he's still stuck.
explain: Be supposed to = it was expected. Example: I'm supposed to be at home.

q: She's bound ___ the science prize. Her project is brilliant.
explain: Be bound to + verb = certain to. Example: It's bound to rain.

q: ___ the instructions carefully, she assembled the telescope in minutes.
explain: Having + p.p. = first action before the main one. Example: Having eaten, we set off.

notes.Being read: Being read is passive: she was read.
notes.Read: Read alone is ambiguous here and sounds passive.
notes.To have read: To have read doesn't start this clause.

q: The lesson ___, the students rushed to the playground.
explain: Absolute construction: noun + adjective/participle. Example: The work done, we relaxed.

notes.was over: Was over would need a conjunction: When the lesson was over.

q: ___ from space, the Great Barrier Reef looks like a ribbon.
explain: Past participle clause = passive: when it is seen. Example: Viewed from above, the town is tiny.

notes.Seeing: Seeing would mean the reef is looking.
notes.Having seen: Having seen means the reef saw something.

q: There being no wind, the sailing race ___ cancelled.
explain: There being = because there was. Example: There being no bus, we walked.

notes.being: Being can't be the main verb.
notes.is being: Is being is present, but this is a past event.

q: All things ___, the school fair was a big success.
explain: All things considered = after thinking about everything. Example: All things considered, it went well.

notes.considering: Considering is used differently: Considering the rain, …
notes.to consider: To consider doesn't fit this fixed phrase.

q: ___ how tired we were, we did well to finish the hike.
explain: Considering + noun/clause = when you think about. Example: Considering his age, he's very tall.

notes.Considered: Considered is the fixed phrase with 'all things'.
notes.To consider: To consider doesn't start a clause like this.

q: The ___ of the new library has been delayed again.
explain: Nominalisation: verb → noun to make writing more formal. Example: The arrival of the train.

notes.open: Open is a verb or adjective.

q: Her ___ to give up inspired the whole team.
explain: Refuse → refusal (noun). Example: His refusal to help surprised us.

notes.refusing: Refusing is a gerund, but refusal is the natural noun here.

q: The fact ___ nobody noticed the dragon is astonishing.
explain: The fact that + clause. Example: The fact that it's free helps.

notes.which: Which would make it a relative clause, which doesn't fit.

q: ___ hard she tried, she couldn't open the treasure chest.
explain: However + adjective/adverb + subject + verb = no matter how. Example: However fast he ran, he was late.

notes.Although: Although can't go before hard like this.
notes.Whatever: Whatever is for things: whatever she did.

q: ___ his fear of heights, he climbed to the top of the tower.
explain: Notwithstanding + noun = despite (formal). Example: Notwithstanding the rain, we played.

notes.Albeit: Albeit is followed by an adjective or adverb, not a noun phrase.
notes.Nonetheless: Nonetheless is an adverb used after a full sentence.

q: The plan was clever, ___ a little risky.
explain: Albeit + adjective = although (formal). Example: He agreed, albeit reluctantly.

q: Some owls hunt at night, ___ others are active by day.
explain: Whereas = contrast between two facts. Example: I like cats, whereas my sister likes dogs.

notes.albeit: Albeit is followed by an adjective.
notes.nevertheless: Nevertheless starts a new idea, usually after a full stop.

q: We'll go stargazing ___ the sky is clear.
explain: Providing/provided (that) = only if. Example: You can come providing you're quiet.

notes.lest: Lest means in case (formal) and needs should.

q: Keep the cage locked ___ the parrot escape again.
explain: Lest + (should) + base verb = so that … not (formal). Example: Speak quietly lest you wake her.

notes.so that: So that would need a negative: so that it doesn't escape.

q: ___ the forecast, the comet should be visible tonight.
explain: According to = as said by. Example: According to Mia, the test is easy.

notes.Thanks for: Thanks for is used when thanking.

q: The launch was delayed ___ a fault in the rocket's engine.
explain: Owing to / due to + noun = because of. Example: Owing to the rain, we stayed in.

notes.according to: According to means as said by.
notes.in spite: In spite needs of and means despite.

q: ___ the fact that she was the youngest, she led the expedition.
explain: Despite the fact that + clause. Example: Despite the fact that it rained, we went.

notes.In spite: In spite needs of: in spite of the fact.
notes.Although: Although doesn't go before the fact that.

q: By the time the rescue team arrives, the climbers ___ in the cave for two days.
explain: Future perfect continuous: duration up to a future point. Example: By June, I'll have been learning for a year.

notes.will wait: Will wait doesn't show duration up to then.
notes.have been waiting: Have been waiting is up to now, not a future point.

q: I ___ to ask you: can I borrow your telescope?
explain: Past continuous for polite requests. Example: I was hoping you could help.

notes.wonder: Wonder sounds more direct than the polite form.
notes.had wondered: Had wondered suggests you stopped wondering.

q: The museum ___ renovated when we visited, so half of it was closed.
explain: Past continuous passive: was/were being + p.p. Example: The road was being repaired.

notes.was: Was renovated suggests it was finished.
notes.had been being: Had been being isn't natural English.

q: She ___ for the competition for months, so she was exhausted.
explain: Past perfect continuous: an activity up to a past moment. Example: He had been running, so he was out of breath.

notes.has been training: Has been is up to now, not a past moment.

q: The penguins ___ to the sea every spring for thousands of years.
explain: Present perfect continuous: a repeated activity from the past to now. Example: People have been telling this story for centuries.

q: The ___ you practise, the more natural it feels.
explain: The + comparative …, the + comparative. Example: The sooner, the better.

q: This puzzle is ___ harder than the last one.
explain: Considerably/far/much + comparative. Example: far better, much bigger.

notes.too: Too doesn't go before comparatives with than.
notes.so: So doesn't go before comparatives with than.

q: She's by ___ the fastest runner in our year.
explain: By far + superlative. Example: It's by far the best film.

notes.much: We don't say by much + superlative.

q: Hardly ___ of the students had heard of the comet.
explain: Hardly any = almost none. Example: There's hardly any milk left.

notes.no: Hardly is already negative, so no would make a double negative.

q: ___ student in the class received a certificate.
explain: Every + singular noun. Example: Every child loves stories.

notes.All: All needs a plural noun: all students.
notes.Each of: Each of needs the: each of the students.

q: Not ___ of the rumours about the haunted tower were true.
explain: Not all of = some weren't. Example: Not all of us agreed.

notes.every: Every can't be followed by of.
notes.each: Each of needs a singular verb: was.
notes.much: Much is for uncountable nouns; rumours are countable.

q: The rain prevented us ___ the summit.
explain: Prevent/stop someone from + -ing. Example: Nothing will stop me from trying.

notes.reaching to: Reaching to adds a wrong preposition.
notes.for reaching: Prevent goes with from, not for.

q: I object ___ treated like a little kid!
explain: Object to + -ing (to is a preposition). Example: I object to waiting.

notes.to be: To here is a preposition, so we need -ing.
notes.for being: Object goes with to, not for.

q: She succeeded ___ the ancient code.
explain: Succeed in + -ing. Example: He succeeded in escaping.

notes.at crack: Succeed goes with in, and we need -ing.

q: The guide urged us ___ close together in the forest.
explain: Urge someone to do something. Example: She urged me to apply.

q: He's thinking ___ joining the robotics club.
explain: Think about/of + -ing. Example: I'm thinking of learning Japanese.

q: We were made ___ the whole poem by heart.
explain: Make + object + base verb (active), but be made + to-infinitive (passive). Example: He was made to wait.

notes.learn: In the passive, made needs to.

q: I can't help but ___ that the cat is planning something.
explain: Can't help but + base verb. Example: I can't help but smile.

notes.feeling: Can't help feeling is right, but after 'but' we use the base form.
notes.to feel: No to after can't help but.

q: The spy was seen ___ the building at midnight.
explain: Active: see someone leave; passive: be seen to leave. Example: He was heard to say…

q: It's no good ___ about the lost match now.
explain: It's no good/use + -ing. Example: It's no use crying.

notes.to complain: It's no good isn't followed by to-infinitive.

q: She has a habit of ___ her pencil when she's thinking.
explain: Noun + of + -ing. Example: the idea of leaving.

q: Rather than ___ the bus, let's cycle to the museum.
explain: Rather than + base verb (or -ing). Example: Rather than wait, we walked.

notes.taking to: Taking to adds an extra to.

q: The task, ___ seemed easy at first, took us all afternoon.
explain: Non-defining relative clause (between commas): which. Example: The film, which was long, was great.

q: The island, ___ only access is by boat, is home to rare tortoises.
explain: Whose can refer to things: the island whose access… Example: a house whose roof leaks.

notes.which: Which would need: to which the only access.
notes.where its: Where its adds an extra possessive.

q: There are several reasons, the most important of ___ is safety.
explain: Quantifier/superlative + of which. Example: three books, one of which is mine.

notes.them: Them would create a run-on sentence.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Little did they know that the map was a fake.
explain: Little + did + subject + verb.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Were it not for the rain, we would be outside.
explain: Were it not for = if it weren't for.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: What surprised me most was how calm she stayed.
explain: What-clause + was + the focus.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Only after the storm passed did we leave the cave.
explain: Only after… + inversion.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: She is said to have trained with the champion.
explain: is said to have + pp.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Hardly had… when (No sooner had… than).

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: It's high time + past simple.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: have + past participle: have I seen.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: whose shows possession: the team whose coach…

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Despite + noun/-ing; Although + a clause (she was tired).

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Should + subject + plain verb: Should you need help…

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: ___ as it may sound, the robot ___ learned to dance.
explain: Adjective + as + it may sound; actually = in fact.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Rarely ___ we seen such a bright comet, ___ the experts say.
explain: Rarely + inversion; 'or so the experts say'.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Had I ___ the instructions, I ___ have broken it.
explain: Had + pp, wouldn't have + pp.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: So ___ was the puzzle that nobody solved it ___ the end of term.
explain: So + adjective + was…; before the end.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Rarely have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
explain: Inversion after a negative adverb: Rarely have I seen.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: What I need is a long holiday.
explain: Cleft sentence: What I need is…

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Had I known, I would have called you.
explain: Inverted third conditional: Had I known = If I had known.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: It was my sister who found the puppy.
explain: It-cleft: It was my sister who…

q: Build the sentence.
answer: She is said to be the best player.
explain: Reporting passive: is said to be.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Were it not for you, I'd be lost.
explain: Inverted conditional: Were it not for = If it weren't for.

q: Build the sentence.
